rationale:
ROUND 2 — answering round 1's REVISE (gated by editquality's HIGH). Every objection was answered with a MEASUREMENT, not an argument, and two of them changed the code.

1. editquality HIGH — the doc_notes subject_type could make P2 a permanent silent no-op. **The objection's mechanism is REAL and its conclusion for this code is false, and it was right to demand I show which.** Measured from pg_constraint 2026-09-03: doc_plans_subject_type_check admits {tool, pipeline, experience, action, experience-pattern, component} (6); doc_notes_subject_type_check admits those SIX PLUS {landmine, decision} (8). So doc_notes' set is a strict SUPERSET of doc_plans' today, 'tool' is in both, and this branch is gated on subjectType=='tool' anyway. I had not stated it and my own 8-point risk section never raised it, which is the fair hit. CHANGED IN CODE: the constraint pair and the superset relation are now recorded at the call site with the caveat that the superset is NOT guaranteed (add a type to doc_plans alone and this goes quiet); the non-fatal warning now names doc_notes_subject_type_check as the first thing to check, because that log line is the only artefact that will exist if the rule has gone silent; and the test now CAPTURES the subject_type and the categories rather than AnyArg-ing them. Both new assertions were mutation-proved: filing under 'experience' goes RED, and a typo'd category goes RED. Stated plainly because it bounds the claim: sqlmock cannot see a CHECK constraint, so the test pins the value being SENT and cannot prove the DB would accept it — the pg_constraint measurement is what does that.

2. editquality LOW — is doc_context.criteria_json really where criteria live? **Verified, and it is not a hopeful default.** The live tool-acceptance-agent config sets criteria_field: 'doc_context.criteria_json' EXPLICITLY on the judge step this edit touches, and on request_browser_run; load_docs (action load_doc_context) writes output_field 'doc_context'. Stronger still, it is self-evidencing: request_browser_run SKIPS the dispatch entirely when that path is empty, so the existence of any Tier-4 PASS to label proves the path is populated — if it were wrong, no browser run would ever have been dispatched and there would be nothing for this edit to label.

3. reuse_agent MEDIUM — proof-of-search rather than inference. **Done, and it was the right ask.** Exactly THREE Go types decode a criteria fence's checks array: discovery_checks/check_tool_acceptance.go:332 (unexported, other package, and does NOT decode expect_values at all — Tier 2 skips computed_values, so it cannot answer this question); internal/adapters/browserrunner/run_checks_action.go:214 (the only decoder that reads ExpectValues — unexported, different top-level tree, and exporting the runner's private decode struct to serve a reporting concern is the wrong direction); and this new file. A grep for exported *Doc/*Check types across both packages returns only discovery-check registrations, never a fence decoder. criteriaFactsFromValue reads the fence-level facts key and never walks checks. ValidateExperienceCriteria is ruled out for the reason write_doc_plan_action.go already records in its own comment — it would reject a tool PLAN for absent checks/binding_schema. CHANGED IN CODE: that search is now written into the file's header, with the residual stated honestly (this is a FOURTH place that knows how to read a fence; what keeps it honest is that both consumers call this one function and the fixtures pin the arms an ad-hoc re-implementation gets wrong).

4. reuse_agent LOW — DB-side category vocabulary not searched. **Searched.** Categories in doc_notes matching fence|criteria|assert|weak|value: 'needs_criteria' (120 rows) and 'criteria' (1). Neither is an equivalent: needs_criteria means NO fence exists at all (Tier 2 writes it and stops), which is the opposite state from a fence that exists and asserts nothing. No 'weak_fence' or similar exists.

5. guardian MEDIUM — the three-callers claim was asserted, not verified. **Now verified structurally**, by walking workflow steps for action='write_doc_plan' rather than by substring: experience-planner (persist_plan), experience-register-writer (write_travelling_doc), tool-generator (write_plan). Three, as claimed.

6. guardian LOW — who consumes the judge's result. **Exactly one consumer**: tool-acceptance-agent's 'judge' step, output_field 'acceptance_verdict'. A grep for 'acceptance_verdict' across all non-test Go returns ZERO — nothing reads it in code, so there is no strict/allow-list mapping for a new key to break.

7. guardian LOW — no lint prevents a future ad-hoc re-implementation. Accepted as a residual and stated in the file rather than papered over. The mitigation shipped is the fixture set: the two arms an ad-hoc parser gets wrong (crediting an empty expect_values by TYPE; not counting `select` as driving) are pinned in BOTH the Go test and the new detector's --self-test, so a divergent second implementation surfaces as a failing fixture rather than as silent drift.

8. The 'missing' note — the root cause has no covering edit. Correct, and deliberate: see the original rationale. It is now also sequenced in writing (bugs_open/449 §8e) behind bugs_open/441, because runComputedValues fails-not-skips on a missing element, so authoring value assertions while 441 is live converts silent blindness into loud FALSE failures aimed at tool-improver.

ALSO NEW IN THIS ROUND, and it is why edit 5 exists: the detector is now SCHEDULED. A detector nobody runs is this estate's documented failure mode ('detection works; schedule and dispatch do not'), so the bash script from the first round has been REPLACED by a Python one on the listing-class-promise-check pattern — one file that a session runs by hand and the clock runs in-cluster (dual-mode _psql_argv) — plus a CronJob, applied and PROVEN end-to-end: pod exit 0, and the doc_notes row it wrote is on record (241 fences graded, 58 driving-and-blind fleet-wide, 13 new in the window). Its --self-test pins the deployed copy against the repo file, and that guard was mutation-proved too.

bugs_open/449. The acceptance ladder implements a check type that compares NUMBERS (computed_values), and the two agents that author fences have never been told it exists. Measured first-hand 2026-09-03 over live doc_plans: tool-generator has written 186 current tool fences, 115 assert no expected value of any kind, ZERO use computed_values, and max(created_at) is TODAY -- so this is a live intake, not a backlog (+16 fences and +8 blind ones in 24h). The cause is one place: the compose_plan prompt enumerates a closed vocabulary and ends 'No other check type exists for interactions'.

THIS SUBMISSION DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIX THE CAUSE, and the ordering is the main thing I want reviewed. The obvious move -- teach the generator the type -- is UNSAFE as written, and the bug says so itself ('an emitted value is not an expected value'). computed_values is a REGRESSION check by construction: its own docstring says values 'are CAPTURED from the tool while it is known good and then defended', and that 'a golden captured from an already-wrong tool pins the wrong answer'. At generation time there is no known-good state, and the generator is handed the tool's own HTML, so any expectation it derives shares a failure mode with the implementation it polices. That is the bugs_open/224 + 225 class: an expired 625k FTB SDLT cap certified green for sixteen months. Separately, bugs_open/441 is (in its owning lane's own re-framing today) a LIVE GENERATOR of stale fences, and runComputedValues fails rather than skips on a missing element by design -- so authoring value assertions today would convert silent blindness into loud FALSE failures aimed at tool-improver.

So this ships the two halves that are strictly additive and cannot create a false failure: the verdict stops overclaiming, and the write door records a blind fence where it is born. The authoring change is planned as a later, separately-reviewed phase after 441 lands.

Why the verdict is the highest-value half: it is the only change that covers all 186 existing fences at once, today, with no backfill and no author cooperation, and it cannot go stale -- the grade is derived from the fence at run time, so a fence that gets weaker gets a weaker verdict with nobody remembering anything. It changes no outcome: a passing tool still passes.

Three design choices I most want challenged: (1) RECORD rather than REFUSE at the door -- I judged that refusing strands the tool, because a tool with no PLAN is inert at BOTH tiers, which is worse than a weak fence; (2) THREE grades rather than two -- collapsing 'pattern' (a hand-authored text_matches) into either 'exact' or 'none' is a lie in one direction or the other, and 449 section 2 corrected itself on exactly this point; (3) the trigger is read off the FENCE (a fill or select step = the tool takes input) rather than from any classifier for 'is this a calculator', because a guarantee conditional on a classifier inherits the classifier's gaps.

plan.summary: bugs_open/449: the platform has a check type that compares NUMBERS (computed_values) and neither fence-authoring agent has ever been told it exists. Measured 2026-09-03 on live doc_plans: tool-generator has written 186 current tool fences, 115 assert no expected value of any kind, ZERO use computed_values, and the newest was created TODAY -- a live intake, not a backlog. So a calculator that prints a confidently wrong figure passes Tier 4 and its record reads PASSED. This change does NOT fix the cause (that is a later, separately reviewed phase -- see the rationale for why teaching the generator today would pin garbage and, with 441 live, produce loud FALSE failures). It ships the two strictly-additive halves: (1) the Tier-4 PASS verdict now states the SCOPE of its own claim -- a pass on a fence that compares nothing is reported as liveness_only, in the doc_note a human reads and the result a machine reads; (2) the single write door that every generated fence passes through records a doc_note when a fence DRIVES the tool's inputs and then asserts no value. No outcome changes: a passing tool still passes. Value: (1) covers all 186 existing fences at once, today, with no backfill and no author cooperation, and cannot go stale because the grade is derived from the fence at run time.

edits.rationale: The single definition of 'this fence compares a value', shared by the judge that reports a verdict and the door that accepts a fence -- one definition rather than two, for the reason criteriaFactsFromValue states beside it in this same package ('so the two cannot disagree'). Grades none/pattern/exact. FAIL-OPEN: an unparseable fence yields Parsed=false and is never reported as 'asserts nothing', because Tier 2 already owns criteria_unparseable and a second weaker report of it would be noise. DrivesInputs is read off the fence's own fill/select steps rather than from a classifier over tool kinds.

P1, the highest-value half. The Tier-4 PASS path now states the scope of its own verdict, in the doc_note a human reads and in the action result a machine reads. Changes no outcome -- a passing tool still passes -- it removes the overclaim. Covers all 186 fences at once with no backfill, and cannot go stale because the grade is derived from the fence at run time.
edits.sketch:
// inside `if allPassed {`
passCriteria := datahelpers.ExtractNestedFieldString(params.CollectedData,
    datahelpers.GetStringField(config, "criteria_field", "doc_context.criteria_json"))
assertions := summariseCriteriaValueAssertions(passCriteria)
...
body := fmt.Sprintf(`## Tier-4 acceptance PASSED -- %s
Observed: ...
Scope of this verdict: %s
Root cause: %s
...`, ..., criteriaAssertionPhrase(assertions), ...)
...
out := map[string]interface{}{ ..., "assertion_grade": assertions.Grade(), "value_assertions": assertions.Total(), "exact_value_assertions": assertions.Exact }
if assertions.AssertsNoValue() { out["verdict_scope"] = "liveness_only" }  // present ONLY in the state worth acting on, so a consumer branches on presence

edits.rationale: P2. The one door every GENERATED fence passes through records a blind fence where it is born, naming the authoring agent. RECORDS, does not refuse: a tool with no PLAN is inert at both tiers, so a refusal today would trade a blind check for no check. Written AFTER the commit -- a note about a PLAN that failed to write would record a document that does not exist -- and non-fatal, because the PLAN is the caller's deliverable and an observation about it must not cost the document. The fence is now extracted ONCE and shared with the existing facts gate, since two extractions are two chances to disagree about which ```criteria block is the fence.

The bug's bar is that a fix which only adds passing checks is indistinguishable from no fix, so every test names the mutation that must turn it red and every silence assertion is paired with a DEMAND CONTROL in the same test. All three mutations were RUN, not merely described: (1) delete the judge's scope line -> TestJudgePass_OnAValuelessFenceReportsLivenessOnly and TestJudgePass_PatternAssertionIsGradedBetweenTheTwo went RED; (2) delete the door's block -> TestWriteDocPlan_RecordsAFenceThatDrivesInputsAndAssertsNothing went RED; (3) credit computed_values by TYPE instead of by having expectations -> the empty-expect_values subtest went RED. Files then restored byte-identically (diff -q) and re-verified green.

edits.rationale: The standing report, and the reason it is scheduled rather than a script: a detector nobody runs is this estate's documented failure mode. Replaces the first round's bash version — one Python file that a session runs by hand (kubectl exec) and the CronJob runs in-cluster (direct psql), chosen by environment, so there is no second implementation of the QUERY. The WINDOW is the headline, not the total, because the standing stock does not rewrite itself and a totals-only report reads as 'no improvement' for a month after a working fix. Ships with base/check.py (a copy the configMapGenerator needs) PINNED by --self-test, an 8-fixture grading suite mirroring the Go test's arms, and a demand control phrased over the PROPERTY (some author still shows computed_values) after the first version was pinned to a lane NAME that changed the same morning — logged in WRONG_CALLS.

plan.risks:
WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK, in the order I think it matters.

1. RECORD vs REFUSE at the door. I chose record. The argument: a tool with NO PLAN is inert at BOTH tiers (Tier 2 writes needs_criteria and stops, Tier 4 emits nothing), so refusing a blind fence today trades a weak check for no check, and the authoring side cannot yet satisfy a refusal. If you think refusal is right now rather than after the prompt phase, say so -- I have written it up as a deferred P5 with its opening trigger stated (when the created_at-windowed count shows the intake has stopped), specifically so it does not become an 'inert until X' line nobody revisits.

2. A NEW doc_note CATEGORY ('fence_asserts_no_value') is a shared-vocabulary addition. Under the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 section 1 I judge it NOT architecture-scope: it changes nothing any shared mechanism GUARANTEES, it has no automated consumer today, and nothing reads it until something is written to name it. Enumerated rather than asserted: grep for the category across Go returns only this writer. If a seat disagrees, the remedy is an RFC, not a resubmission with better measurements.

3. VOLUME. The door note fires per PLAN WRITE, and 55 of 186 current fences would qualify today. There is NO cooldown, deliberately -- unlike Tier 2's needs_criteria, which has a 30-day per-subject one -- because a PLAN write is not a sweep: it happens when an agent authors a document, so the note rate is the authoring rate, and one note per authored blind fence is the intended signal. If a reviewer thinks a supersede storm could make that noisy (install_fences.py-style rewrites bypass this door, but a re-generation wave would not), a per-subject cooldown is the obvious mitigation and I would rather add it now than discover it.

4. FAIL-OPEN CORRECTNESS. An unparseable fence yields Parsed=false, is never reported as 'asserts nothing', and produces no note -- Tier 2 already owns criteria_unparseable and a second, weaker report of it would be noise. Check I have not created a path where a parse regression silently presents as a corpus finding.

5. THE THREE GRADES. I refused to collapse 'pattern' (a hand-authored text_matches) into either neighbour. 449 section 2 records that its own first version overclaimed here, and runComputedValues' docstring records the opposite error. If a seat thinks two grades are enough, the case to beat is that /GBP[\d,]+\.\d\d/ is satisfied by the 0.00 an unwired tool prints.

6. WHAT THIS CANNOT DO, stated so nobody quotes it as more: the door governs every GENERATED fence and NO hand-installed one -- operator scripts write doc_plans over psql and bypass the action entirely. That is the right way round (the hand-installed fences are the ones that already assert values) but it is not a total guarantee and I have not described it as one anywhere in the code comments.

7. BLAST RADIUS. write_doc_plan is called by three live agents (tool-generator, experience-planner, experience-register-writer); only the subject_type=='tool' path is touched, so every other PLAN write is byte-identical -- pinned by TestWriteDocPlan_NonToolSubjectIsUntouched. ZERO optional keys added: audit-optional-key-budget.sh puts write_doc_plan at 8 of the RFC_022 budget of 10, and spending two would land it AT the budget and owe an accumulated-surface review.

8. VERIFICATION ALREADY DONE, so you can check my working rather than take it: all three mutations were RUN and went red where predicted (judge scope line deleted; door block deleted; computed_values credited by type), then the files were restored byte-identically (diff -q) and re-verified green. scripts/verify-head-builds.sh with all four files overlaid on HEAD 48bd6c5b6 reports 'ok' for platform/orchestration/actions. The one failing test in that run, discovery_checks/TestStylesheetGutted_TokenSetMatchesCanonicalCSSTokens, is PRE-EXISTING at HEAD in a package this change never touches -- it is the 458 lane's paired-ink token work, and I have verified it fails with my change absent.
